analysis: Examined the cluster runtime facts v2 schema, the new ClusterPublicModels declaration and the pair-serving grant changes. The facts now carry per-model pair-serving grants and parity qualifications. They are strictly parsed: exact field sets, duplicate-key detection, 64 KiB cap, digest and nonzero checks, qualification shape checks, and derived-ID length limits. The strict-parse code looks sound. The main security change moves public-cluster serving eligibility for two models (GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B) from per-record evidence to an in-source owner declaration. It emits constant evidence digest, qualifiedAt and promotable:true, and derives the numerics class from the shipped metallib plus hardcoded hardware. This is reported as a finding (weakened qualification binding, related to T-054/T-056/A-017). The request envelope is also derived from a local catalog.json file (bounded at 4 KiB, keys and id checked) and can enable vision/video. That file is not bound to the artifact hash beyond its model ID, so the release-lane environment must be trusted. publicTrafficLine now reports 'qualified for public traffic' from declared families; this is display-only, and the coordinator remains decisive. Not verifiable from the supplied evidence: the coordinator derivation and validation of these facts, the release-registration authentication (A-005), the test tying the evidence digest to the doc, and whether cluster hops add plaintext exposure of consumer prompts to a second provider. The threat model lacks cluster/public-pair coverage. Recommend a human check of the coordinator side and a threat-model update for the cluster public-serving boundary.

findings.detail: parityQualifications() (ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift:331-333) hardcodes promotable:true, diverged:false, a constant evidenceSHA256 and a constant qualifiedAt (ClusterPublicModels.swift:46-48). It derives the numerics class from whatever metallib the release ships, combined with the hardcoded 'applegpu_g17d'/macOS 27.0 ranks. Any build whose worker reports the two declared artifact hashes is therefore emitted as parity-qualified for public traffic with a 1M-token envelope. This holds even if the metallib, worker or placement code changed since the 2026-10-31 evidence run. Nothing in the facts ties the qualification to the evidence run's build or digests. The evidence digest is also not the records digest used for non-declared grants (evidenceSHA256()). The only link is a test that the constant equals the hash of a doc. A coordinator that derives approvals from these facts (outside the supplied evidence) will treat the claim as qualification. Impact: a regressed or divergent numerics build can be admitted to serve public consumers. Fix: bind the qualification to the qualified metallib/worker/placement digests, or require the coordinator to check them against allowlisted evidence-run digests. Re-run the parity evidence on metallib changes.
findings.title: Public-traffic parity qualifications are asserted from compile-time constants for any build, not bound to evidence for that build
